title: Birria Tacos
description: Braised chuck roast birria with a blended guajillo-ancho-arbol chili consommé, served in cheese-crisped corn tortillas dipped in the braising liquid, topped with onion and cilantro.
equipment: large heavy pot or Dutch oven
cast iron or carbon steel pan

vegetarian.notes: Beef chuck is structural — the braise and consommé are built entirely around it. No vegetarian adaptation is practical for this dish.

steps.title: Season and cube the chuck
steps.text: Cut {i01} into smaller cubes. Season all sides heavily with {i02} and {i03}.

steps.title: Sear the beef in batches
steps.text: Heat {i04} in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat until shimmering. Working in batches to avoid crowding, sear {i01} on all sides until deeply browned, about 2–3 minutes per side. Remove seared beef and set aside; leave the brown bits in the pot. Repeat until all beef is seared.

steps.title: Prep and clean dried chilies
steps.text: Slice the stems off {i08}, {i09}, and {i10}. Run a finger down each chili to open it up and shake or scrape out all the seeds until each is clean.

steps.title: Boil vegetables and chilies
steps.text: In the same pot (no need to clean it), add {i05}, {i06}, {i07}, {i08}, {i09}, {i10}, {i11}, and {i12}. Pour in enough water to cover everything. Bring to a boil and cook for about 10 minutes until all the vegetables and chilies are soft.

steps.title: Blend the chili sauce
steps.text: Remove everything from the pot and transfer to a blender — discard the bay leaves ({i11}). Reserve {i13} from the cooking liquid; discard the rest. Add {i13}, {i14}, and {i15} to the blender. Blend until completely smooth.

steps.title: Strain sauce over the beef
steps.text: Return the seared {i01} to the pot. Strain the blended chili sauce through a fine mesh strainer over the beef, pressing with a spoon to extract all the liquid. Add {i16} and stir to combine.

steps.title: Braise covered on low
steps.text: Bring the pot to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 3.5 to 4 hours, until the meat is completely fall-apart tender. A bright red consommé layer will form on top.

steps.title: Shred the beef and soak
steps.text: Remove the beef and shred it — you can use your hands or two forks. Return the shredded meat to the broth and let it sit for at least a couple of minutes (longer is better) so it soaks up the consommé flavor.

steps.title: Dip tortillas and fill
steps.text: Skim the bright red consommé fat from the top of the broth into a separate bowl (this is for dipping). Dip each {i17} into the fat/consommé layer, then lay in a hot pan. Add {i18} to one half, then pile on shredded {i01}, chopped {i19}, and {i20}. Fold the tortilla over.

steps.title: Pan-fry until crispy
steps.text: Cook the filled tacos in a pan over medium to medium-high heat, flipping once, until both sides are golden and crispy and the cheese is melted. Serve immediately with consommé on the side for dipping.
